# The Complete Apparel Sourcing Guide for Small Businesses in India

URL: https://vozcruda.com/apparel-sourcing-guide.html
Updated: 2026-10-24

**Short answer:** To source apparel in India as a small business: decide your product and match it to the right hub (for example Tiruppur for knitwear), shortlist **full-package manufacturers** or a sourcing partner, ask about MOQ, lead time and sampling, approve a **pre-production sample**, and confirm everything in a written purchase order with staged payments. If your quantity is below the factory minimum, order fewer styles or pool your order with other buyers.

If you're running a small fashion business in India — whether you're selling on Instagram, listing on Meesho or Myntra, or building your own D2C brand — apparel sourcing is probably your biggest operational challenge. Finding the right manufacturer, negotiating terms, managing quality, and keeping your supply chain moving is genuinely hard when you're not placing lakhs of units.

This guide covers the full picture: the landscape, the terminology, how to find and evaluate manufacturers, what to do about MOQs, and how to build a sourcing system that works as your business grows.

## Why Apparel Sourcing Is Hard for Small Businesses

India has one of the world's largest apparel manufacturing ecosystems — Tirupur, Surat, Jaipur, Delhi, Mumbai, Ludhiana — and yet most small businesses struggle to access it properly. The reasons are structural.

### Manufacturers are built for large buyers

Most apparel factories in India optimise for high-volume, repeat buyers: large exporters, big retail chains, and e-commerce giants. Their pricing, processes, and minimum order quantities (MOQs) are calibrated for buyers placing 500–5,000 units minimum. A small retailer ordering 30 pieces of a cotton kurta simply isn't their priority.

### Information is fragmented

Unlike in some other industries, there's no single, reliable directory of verified Indian apparel manufacturers organised by category, MOQ, and capability. Most sourcing still happens through referrals, trade shows like Texworld and India ITME, or WhatsApp groups — which are great if you're already in the network, and nearly useless if you're not.

### Quality and reliability vary significantly

Two manufacturers in the same city producing the same garment category can have dramatically different quality standards, timelines, and communication norms. Without a proper vetting process, a small business can lose significant money on a bad order — and not have the volume to negotiate a resolution.

"The garment industry is not difficult to access because of a lack of manufacturers. It's difficult to access because of a lack of reliable sourcing infrastructure for buyers who aren't placing large volumes."

## Understanding the Types of Apparel Manufacturers

Before you start reaching out to suppliers, it helps to understand who you're actually dealing with. The apparel supply chain in India involves several distinct types of businesses, each with different capabilities and minimums.

### Fabric mills

These produce raw fabric — cotton, linen, polyester, blends. You won't typically source directly from mills unless you're doing full custom fabric development, which requires significant volumes (usually 500m+ per colour/weave). For most small businesses, fabric is the manufacturer's problem to source.

### CMT manufacturers (Cut, Make, Trim)

CMT factories take your fabric and patterns and produce finished garments. You're responsible for sourcing fabric, designing patterns, and providing trims (buttons, zips, labels). CMT is common for businesses with strong design capabilities and established fabric relationships. MOQs can be lower — sometimes 50–100 pieces — but coordination complexity is higher.

### Full-package manufacturers

Full-package suppliers handle the entire process: fabric sourcing, cutting, stitching, finishing, and packing. You provide a tech pack or sample, they handle the rest. This is the most common model for small businesses because it reduces operational complexity. MOQs are typically higher — 200–1,000 units — because the manufacturer is bearing more coordination cost.

### Trading companies and sourcing agents

These are intermediaries who don't own factories but work with a network of manufacturers. They can reduce sourcing friction significantly, especially for businesses without established factory relationships. The trade-off is an additional margin on your cost price — typically 8–15%.

Which type should you use?

For most small businesses just starting out: full-package manufacturers or a sourcing partner with a verified network. Once you have consistent volume and clearer product specs, moving to CMT can reduce cost per unit — but that's a later optimisation.

## MOQ Explained — and How to Work Around It

**MOQ (Minimum Order Quantity)** is the minimum number of units a manufacturer requires before they'll accept an order. It exists because production setup — cutting patterns, calibrating machines, sourcing fabric in required quantities — has a fixed cost that needs to be spread across enough units to be economical.

### Typical MOQs in Indian apparel manufacturing

- **Knitwear (t-shirts, polos, basic tees):** 50–200 units per style per colour
- **Woven tops, kurtas, shirts:** 100–300 units per style
- **Denim:** 200–500 units (fabric MOQs are high)
- **Outerwear, blazers, structured garments:** 200–500 units
- **Ethnic wear (sarees, lehengas, heavy embroidery):** Often lower MOQs but longer lead times

### Strategies for managing MOQs as a small buyer

There are four main approaches, and the right one depends on your business model:

- **Focus on fewer SKUs, deeper inventory.** Instead of sourcing 20 styles at 30 units each, source 3 styles at 200 units each. This is less exciting but much more operationally manageable and typically produces better unit economics.
- **Join an MOQ aggregation platform.** Platforms like Voz Cruda pool sourcing demand from multiple small buyers to collectively meet a manufacturer's MOQ. You order 30 pieces; the platform aggregates demand from other buyers for the same style, and the factory sees the full order. This is one of the most effective ways to access quality manufacturing without the volume constraint.
- **Negotiate with padding flexibility.** Some manufacturers will accept lower MOQs if you agree to pay a slightly higher per-unit cost (a "small order surcharge") or commit to repeat orders on a schedule. This works best once you've established a relationship.
- **Start with stock-lot buying.** Many manufacturers have excess fabric or finished goods from cancelled orders. Buying from stock — not custom production — has no MOQ in the traditional sense. The trade-off is limited style/colour control.

## How to Find Reliable Manufacturers

This is where most small business owners spend too much time without a clear methodology. Here's a structured approach.

### Know your category and location before searching

India's manufacturing hubs specialise. Searching for a manufacturer without understanding the geography wastes time and often leads to mismatches:

- **Tirupur (Tamil Nadu):** Knitwear capital of India — t-shirts, hoodies, activewear, basics
- **Surat (Gujarat):** Synthetic fabrics, woven garments, sarees, dress materials
- **Jaipur (Rajasthan):** Block print, ethnic wear, hand-worked garments, artisan production
- **Delhi NCR:** Wide variety — fast fashion, woven, export-oriented; Chandni Chowk for fabrics
- **Mumbai:** Export garments, denim, western wear; Dharavi for lower-cost production
- **Ludhiana (Punjab):** Knitwear, woollens, hosiery

### Where to actually find manufacturers

- **Trade shows:** Texworld India, IIGF (India International Garment Fair), and regional textile expos are the highest-quality sourcing environments. Manufacturers attend specifically to meet buyers.
- **IndiaMART and TradeIndia:** Useful starting points, but verify everything — listings are not curated and quality varies enormously.
- **Sourcing platforms and agents:** Reduces search time significantly if you work with someone with verified supplier relationships.
- **Referrals from other sellers:** Often the most reliable signal. Fashion seller communities on WhatsApp, Telegram, and LinkedIn can be valuable.
- **Direct visits:** For anything beyond a trial order, visiting a factory before placing a significant order is worth the cost. You see the actual production environment, workforce, and equipment.

### Initial qualification questions to ask

When you first contact a manufacturer, ask:

- What product categories do you specialise in?
- What is your MOQ per style per colour?
- What is your typical lead time from order confirmation to dispatch?
- Do you offer sampling? What is the sample cost and lead time?
- Do you work with domestic buyers or only export?
- Can you share references or previous work?

## Quality Checks and Sampling

Never place a production order without first going through a proper sampling process. This is the most common mistake small businesses make — skipping sampling to save time or cost, and then receiving a production run that doesn't match expectations.

### The sampling process

- **Proto / development sample:** First version of the garment. Likely not in the correct fabric. Used to validate the design and construction. Expect 2–4 rounds of revision.
- **Pre-production sample (PP sample):** Made in the actual production fabric and trims, in the actual colourway. This is the sample you approve before production begins. Do not skip this.
- **Production sample (TOP — Top of Production):** Taken from the start of the actual production run. Confirms that what's on the line matches your approved PP sample.

### What to check in every sample

- Measurements against your size spec / tech pack
- Fabric feel, weight, and shrinkage (wash the sample before approving)
- Stitching quality — stitch density, seam strength, no skipped stitches
- Colourway — check against your reference in natural light
- Finishing — hems, buttons, zips, labels, packaging

Practical tip

Always wash your approved sample before signing off on it. Many quality issues — shrinkage, colour bleeding, fabric pilling — only become apparent after a wash cycle. A garment that looks perfect off the production line but shrinks two sizes after the first wash is a returns problem waiting to happen.

## Placing Your First Order

Once you've approved a sample and decided to proceed, there are several things to get right before production starts.

### Document everything in writing

Your purchase order (PO) should specify: style name and code, size breakdown, quantity per size, colour, fabric specs, trim details, construction notes, per-unit price, total order value, payment terms, delivery date, and packaging requirements. Verbal agreements are not orders.

### Payment terms

The standard for domestic production in India is typically **30–50% advance** at order confirmation, and the balance before or at dispatch. For a first order with a new manufacturer, expect to pay a higher advance — it's normal and appropriate given there's no established relationship. Do not pay 100% upfront.

### Lead times to plan around

- Sampling: 1–3 weeks per round
- Fabric procurement by manufacturer: 2–4 weeks
- Production: 3–6 weeks depending on complexity and order size
- Finishing and dispatch: 3–7 days
- **Total from order confirmation to delivery: typically 6–12 weeks**

This is why inventory planning matters. If you're selling seasonally or reacting to trends, you need to be ordering 2–3 months before you need stock on hand.

## Scaling Your Sourcing Operation

The sourcing processes that work for your first few orders need to evolve as your business grows. Here's what changes at different stages.

### Early stage (₹0–₹25L annual sourcing)

Focus on 1–3 products. Keep SKU count low. Use a sourcing partner or aggregation platform to access manufacturers without meeting high MOQs. Prioritise learning over optimisation — understand what sells before scaling what doesn't.

### Growth stage (₹25L–₹1Cr annual sourcing)

You now have enough volume to start building direct manufacturer relationships. Invest in proper tech packs and standardise your quality requirements. Start tracking supplier performance (lead time adherence, defect rates, communication responsiveness). Consider a second or third supplier to reduce dependency risk.

### Scale stage (₹1Cr+ annual sourcing)

At this level, sourcing becomes a competitive advantage. Invest in sourcing management systems, consider partial vertical integration (owning fabric relationships), and build a structured supplier scorecard process. The brands that win long-term tend to treat their supply chain as a strategic asset, not just a cost centre.

## Common Sourcing Mistakes to Avoid

- **Skipping sampling to save cost or time.** This almost always costs more in the end — whether through returns, dead stock, or lost customer trust.
- **Working with too many suppliers too early.** Each supplier relationship requires coordination effort. Managing five mediocre suppliers is worse than managing two excellent ones.
- **Not accounting for full landed cost.** Compare manufacturers on total cost: per-unit price + freight + packaging + inspection + payment processing — not just the sticker price.
- **Chasing the lowest MOQ at the expense of quality.** A manufacturer who offers 20-piece MOQs is often doing so because they can't fill their capacity with larger buyers. Ask why before you commit.
- **No written purchase orders.** If a dispute arises — wrong colour, wrong size breakdown, late delivery — you need documentation. WhatsApp confirmations are not adequate on their own.
- **Ordering too much too soon.** The most common cash flow killer for small fashion businesses is over-ordering based on optimistic sell-through projections. Start conservatively. Reorder fast if demand is strong.

## Final thoughts

Apparel sourcing in India is genuinely complex — but it's learnable. The businesses that figure it out gain a durable operational advantage over competitors who are still struggling with inconsistent supply, missed deadlines, and quality problems.

The key is to build systems: a small, reliable supplier network; standardised sampling and QC processes; clear written documentation; and realistic lead time planning. These don't require large volumes to implement — just discipline and consistency.

If you're a small or growing apparel business looking for support building this infrastructure — from supplier matching and MOQ aggregation to procurement coordination — [get in touch with Voz Cruda](https://vozcruda.com/#contact). That's exactly what we're building.

## Frequently asked questions

**What is the best way for a small business to source apparel in India?**
Start with a full-package manufacturer or a sourcing partner with a verified network, keep your range to a few styles, approve a pre-production sample, and put every order in a written purchase order. Move to CMT and direct factory relationships once your volume and specs are consistent.

**How can I order clothing below a manufacturer's MOQ?**
Four common routes: focus on fewer styles in deeper quantities, join an MOQ aggregation (order pooling) platform such as Smallotz, negotiate a small order surcharge or a repeat order plan, or buy from stock lots, which trades MOQ for less control over style and colour.

**How long does clothing production take in India?**
From order confirmation to delivery is typically 6 to 12 weeks: sampling takes 1 to 3 weeks per round, fabric procurement 2 to 4 weeks, production 3 to 6 weeks, and finishing and dispatch 3 to 7 days.

**What payment terms are normal with Indian garment manufacturers?**
For domestic production, typically 30 to 50% advance at order confirmation and the balance before or at dispatch. Expect a higher advance on a first order with a new manufacturer.

# Low MOQ Hoodie Manufacturers in India: Custom Hoodies and Sweatshirts in Small Batches

URL: https://vozcruda.com/low-moq-hoodie-manufacturer-india.html
Updated: 2026-10-10

**Short answer:** To make custom hoodies in small quantities in India, choose your fabric (brushed fleece for warmth or French terry for year-round wear), pick a GSM (around 300 for everyday, 350 to 450 for heavyweight streetwear), decide the fit and details, approve a sample, then produce through a low MOQ route. Tiruppur is the main hub, and pooled lots on Smallotz let you order fewer pieces than a factory's usual 200 to 500 minimum.

Hoodies sell at higher prices than tees and carry your brand's look in a big way. They also have more moving parts: fabric, rib, hood construction, drawcords, pockets and fit. Getting those right on a small first order is what this guide is about.

## Fleece or French terry?

| Fabric | Inside feel | Best for | Keep in mind |
|---|---|---|---|
| Brushed fleece | Soft, fluffy, warm | Winter collections, heavyweight streetwear | Too warm for much of India outside winter |
| French terry (loop knit) | Small loops, smooth | Year-round hoodies, sweatshirts, joggers | Less warm, slightly less plush |
| Cotton-polyester blend | Varies | Merch, team wear, value lines | Less shrinkage, less premium feel |

Many Indian brands use French terry for most of the year and fleece for a winter drop. Read more in our [fabric guide for clothing brands](https://vozcruda.com/fabric-guide-for-clothing-brands.html).

## Choosing the GSM

- **240 to 280 GSM:** light sweatshirts and summer hoodies.
- **280 to 320 GSM:** everyday hoodies with a solid feel.
- **350 to 450 GSM:** heavyweight streetwear hoodies that hold their shape.

Heavier fabric costs more and takes longer to dry and finish, so ask for the exact GSM in your quote and check it on the sample.

## Fit and construction details

- **Fit:** regular, oversized with dropped shoulders, or boxy and cropped.
- **Hood:** two-panel or three-panel; single or double layer. A double-layer hood holds shape better.
- **Rib:** cuffs and hem in matching rib, usually 2x2 or 1x1. Ask for rib in the same colour and dye lot.
- **Drawcords:** flat or round, with metal eyelets or stitched holes, or none for a cleaner look.
- **Pocket:** kangaroo pocket, side-seam pockets or none.
- **Finishing:** pre-shrunk or garment-washed fabric reduces shrinkage after the first wash.

## Decoration

Screen printing, puff print and embroidery are the most popular on hoodies. Embroidery suits small chest logos; large back prints work well in screen or DTF. See [screen printing vs DTF vs DTG](https://vozcruda.com/screen-printing-vs-dtf-vs-dtg-india.html) to choose.

## Typical MOQs and what drives them

Hoodie MOQs are often higher than for simple knits because fleece and its matching rib are bought and dyed together in minimum lots. Custom colours add another minimum. Expect factory MOQs of around 200 to 500 pieces per style, and higher if each colour has its own minimum.

## How to order a small batch of hoodies

- Choose fabric, GSM, fit, colour and details, and put them in a [simple tech pack](https://vozcruda.com/tech-pack-guide-for-beginners.html). Our [tech pack example](https://vozcruda.com/tech-pack-example-t-shirt.html) notes what to add for hoodies.
- Join or start a pooled hoodie lot on Smallotz, or request a direct quote for 300+ pieces per style.
- Approve a sample: check GSM, measurements, rib match, hood shape and print.
- Wash-test the sample for shrinkage and pilling.
- Confirm quantity, size split and delivery date in writing. Book winter drops early, as factories get busy before the season.

Ready to make your hoodies? [Open Smallotz](https://smallotz.vozcruda.com/) or [send us your requirement](https://vozcruda.com/#contact).

## Frequently asked questions

**What is the MOQ for custom hoodies in India?**
Many factories ask for 200 to 500 pieces per style for custom hoodies, mainly because fleece fabric and matching rib are bought in minimum lots. Pooled lots on Smallotz let small brands order fewer pieces at close to bulk pricing.

**What GSM is good for a hoodie?**
Everyday hoodies are often 280 to 320 GSM. Heavyweight streetwear hoodies commonly use 350 to 450 GSM fleece or French terry for a thick, structured feel.

**What is the difference between fleece and French terry?**
Both are knitted with a smooth face. Fleece is brushed on the inside for a soft, warm, fluffy feel. French terry keeps small loops on the inside, so it is lighter and more breathable, which suits warmer climates.

**Where are hoodies made in India?**
Tiruppur is the main hub for cotton fleece and French terry hoodies. Ludhiana also produces winterwear and sweatshirts, especially in heavier and blended fabrics.

**Are hoodies a good product for an Indian clothing brand?**
Yes, but demand is seasonal in much of India. Many brands pair heavyweight winter hoodies with lighter French terry versions that sell for more of the year.

# Low MOQ Kidswear Manufacturers in India: How to Start a Kids' Clothing Brand

URL: https://vozcruda.com/low-moq-kidswear-manufacturers-india.html
Updated: 2026-10-10

**Short answer:** To start a kidswear brand with low MOQ in India, focus on one age band, use soft breathable cotton fabrics, build safety into the design (no neck drawcords, secure fastenings, soft labels), and source from a kidswear hub like Tiruppur. Spread a small order across a focused size set, or join a pooled lot to order fewer pieces at near-bulk pricing.

Parents buy kidswear again and again as children grow, which makes it a strong category for a new brand. The catch is that one style needs many sizes, and parents expect comfort and safety without compromise. Both affect how you plan a small first order.

## Pick a focused age band

| Age band | Typical products | What matters most |
|---|---|---|
| 0 to 24 months | Rompers, onesies, jhablas, sets | Softness, easy changing, gentle fastenings |
| 2 to 8 years | Tees, shorts, co-ords, dresses, nightwear | Durability, washability, fun prints |
| 8 to 14 years | Casual and occasion wear | Style that feels grown-up, fit |

Starting with one band keeps sizes, patterns and stock under control.

## Fabrics that work for kids

- **Cotton single jersey:** soft and breathable for tees and dresses.
- **Interlock:** thicker, smoother and stable, popular for baby wear.
- **Rib:** stretchy, good for fitted pieces and leggings.
- **Organic cotton:** a strong selling point with parents, at a higher fabric cost.
- **Muslin and cotton voile:** light wovens for summer and swaddles.

More detail in our [fabric guide](https://vozcruda.com/fabric-guide-for-clothing-brands.html).

## Safety and comfort checklist

- No drawcords at the hood or neck for young children.
- Buttons, snaps and trims attached firmly and pull-tested.
- Flat or covered seams near the skin, with no scratchy edges.
- Soft labels, or printed labels instead of stiff woven tags.
- Skin-safe dyes and print inks, and no small decorations that can come loose.
- Easy openings for babies, such as envelope necks and snap crotches.

Check the labelling and safety rules that apply to children's products where you sell, including on marketplaces.

## Where kidswear is made in India

**Tiruppur** is the largest hub for cotton knit kidswear and baby wear. **Kolkata** makes value kidswear and hosiery. **Delhi NCR** and **Mumbai** have units for occasion wear and woven pieces. See our guide to [India's apparel hubs](https://vozcruda.com/india-apparel-manufacturing-hubs.html).

## Planning a small order across sizes

A style in five sizes needs a size split. Weight it towards the sizes that sell best rather than ordering equal amounts. For example, a 100-piece order of a toddler tee might be split 15, 25, 25, 20 and 15 across five sizes. Track sell-through by size and adjust your next order.

## How to order kidswear in small batches

- Choose your age band and 2 to 4 hero styles.
- Specify fabric, GSM, colours, prints and safety details in a [tech pack](https://vozcruda.com/tech-pack-guide-for-beginners.html).
- Approve a sample in at least two sizes, and wash-test it.
- Order through a pooled lot or a small-batch kidswear unit.
- Inspect fastenings and seams on arrival before selling.

Want help finding the right kidswear manufacturer? [Tell Voz Cruda what you want to make](https://vozcruda.com/#contact).

## Frequently asked questions

**What is the MOQ for kidswear in India?**
Kidswear factories often ask for a few hundred pieces per style, spread across a size set. Because the size range is wide, MOQs per size can be small even when the total is high. Pooled lots can help you start with fewer pieces.

**Which fabric is best for kids' clothing?**
Soft, breathable cotton is the most common choice, especially combed or organic cotton single jersey, interlock and rib for babies. Avoid rough trims and scratchy seams near the skin.

**Where is kidswear made in India?**
Tiruppur is the largest hub for cotton knit kidswear. Kolkata produces value kidswear and hosiery, and Delhi NCR and Mumbai have units for occasion and woven kidswear.

**What safety points matter in children's clothing?**
Avoid drawcords at the neck for young children, secure buttons and snaps firmly, use soft labels or printed labels, choose skin-safe dyes and prints, and check that nothing small can come loose.

**How many sizes should a kidswear brand start with?**
Many brands start with a focused age band, such as 0 to 24 months or 2 to 8 years, rather than every size from newborn to teen. It keeps the first order smaller and the range easier to manage.

# Low MOQ Ethnic Wear Manufacturers in India: Kurtas, Sets and Co-ords in Small Batches

URL: https://vozcruda.com/low-moq-ethnic-wear-manufacturers-india.html
Updated: 2026-10-10

**Short answer:** To source ethnic wear in small batches in India, pick your hub by style (Jaipur for block prints, Surat for synthetic and printed fabrics, Delhi NCR for embroidery and fusion), choose a print method that suits small runs such as digital print, and keep your first drop to a few designs in a focused size range. Ethnic wear MOQs are often 100 to 300 pieces per design, and pooled lots can bring that lower.

Kurtas, kurta sets and ethnic co-ords sell all year in India, with festive and wedding peaks on top. Because much of the industry already works in smaller print and dye batches, ethnic wear is one of the easier categories to start small in.

## Popular products and fabrics

| Product | Common fabrics | Occasion |
|---|---|---|
| Everyday kurtas and kurtis | Cotton, cambric, mulmul, rayon, linen blends | Daily and office wear |
| Kurta sets and co-ords | Cotton, rayon, modal, chanderi | Casual and smart casual |
| Festive kurtas | Georgette, crepe, silk blends, chanderi | Festivals and weddings |
| Men's kurtas | Cotton, linen, silk blends | Daily to festive |

## Choosing a print or decoration method

| Method | Look | Small batch fit |
|---|---|---|
| Hand block print | Handmade, natural variation | Good, but slower |
| Screen print on fabric | Crisp, repeatable | Better at moderate runs |
| Digital print | Unlimited colours, fine detail | Excellent |
| Embroidery and handwork | Premium, festive | Good, cost depends on detail |
| Solid dyed with trims | Minimal | Good if base fabric is shared |

## Where to source

- **Jaipur:** block-printed cottons, kurtas, dresses and sets with a handcrafted feel. Nearby Sanganer and Bagru are known for traditional prints.
- **Surat:** synthetic and blended fabrics, printed dress materials and value ethnic wear.
- **Delhi NCR:** embroidery, embellishment and fusion ethnic wear for brands.

Read more in [India's apparel manufacturing hubs](https://vozcruda.com/india-apparel-manufacturing-hubs.html).

## Ways to keep MOQs low in ethnic wear

- **Share a base fabric** across several designs so fabric minimums are met together.
- **Use digital printing** for multi-colour designs without screens.
- **Limit colourways** on your first drop.
- **Keep sizes focused,** for example S to XXL, before adding plus sizes in a later drop.
- **Pool your order** with other buyers using the same base product.

## Quality points to check on samples

- Colour fastness: wash the sample and check for bleeding, especially with deep dyes.
- Print alignment at seams and panels.
- Shrinkage on cotton and rayon after washing.
- Neckline finish, side slits and hem straightness.
- Lining quality in sheer fabrics.

## Plan around the festive calendar

Festive demand peaks around Diwali and the wedding season. Factories get busy in the weeks before, so place festive orders well ahead and keep everyday styles running year-round.

Ready to launch your ethnic wear line? [Share your requirement with Voz Cruda](https://vozcruda.com/#contact) or [open Smallotz](https://smallotz.vozcruda.com/).

## Frequently asked questions

**What is the MOQ for kurtas in India?**
Ethnic wear MOQs are often lower than for knitwear, commonly around 100 to 300 pieces per design. Printing and dyeing batches drive the minimum, so designs that share a fabric or print can help reach it.

**Which city is best for kurta manufacturing?**
Jaipur is known for block-printed cotton kurtas and handwork, Surat for synthetic and printed fabrics and dress materials, and Delhi NCR for embroidered, embellished and fusion ethnic wear.

**What is the difference between block print and digital print?**
Block printing is done by hand with carved wooden blocks, giving a handmade look with natural variation. Digital printing applies designs from a file, allowing unlimited colours and detail with consistent results and often lower minimums.

**Which fabrics are popular for kurtas?**
Cotton, cambric, mulmul, rayon, linen blends, chanderi and modal are popular for everyday kurtas. Georgette, crepe and silk blends are common for festive wear.

**Can I start an ethnic wear brand with small quantities?**
Yes. Ethnic wear suits small runs, especially with digital printing and shared base fabrics. Starting with a few designs in a tight size range keeps your first order small.

# How to Price Your Clothing Products: Costing, Margins and MRP for Indian Brands

URL: https://vozcruda.com/how-to-price-clothing-products.html
Updated: 2026-10-10

**Short answer:** Price a clothing product from the bottom up: add every cost to get your landed cost per piece, add the costs of selling it (shipping, returns, fees, marketing per order), then apply a markup that leaves real profit. Many D2C brands land at around three to four times landed cost. Finally, check the price against your market and positioning.

## Step 1: Build your landed cost per piece

Landed cost is everything it takes to get one finished, packed piece into your hands.

- Fabric and making (cut, make and trim)
- Printing or embroidery
- Labels, hang tags and trims
- Polybag, mailer box and inserts
- Freight from the factory to you
- Sampling and tech pack costs, spread over the order
- Taxes you cannot recover

## Step 2: Add the cost of selling each order

- **Shipping to the customer**, including cash-on-delivery charges if you offer COD.
- **Payment gateway fees** on prepaid orders.
- **Returns and exchanges:** reverse shipping and repacking, spread across kept orders.
- **Marketplace commission** and fees if you sell on platforms.
- **Marketing cost per order:** ad spend and creator costs divided by orders.

## Step 3: A worked example

The figures below are illustrative, to show the method. Use your own quotes.

| Line | Per piece (₹) |
|---|---|
| Heavyweight tee, made and printed | 300 |
| Labels, tags and packaging | 40 |
| Freight and sampling, spread over order | 20 |
| Landed cost | 360 |
| Shipping, gateway and returns per order | 120 |
| Marketing per order | 250 |
| Total cost to sell one | 730 |
| Selling price at 3.5x landed cost | 1,260 |
| Profit per order before overheads and tax | 530 |

Notice how much marketing and fulfilment add. A brand that priced at 2x landed cost (₹720) would lose money on every order once marketing is included.

Run your own numbers in the free [clothing cost and price calculator](https://vozcruda.com/clothing-cost-calculator.html). It uses this exact method and shows your landed cost, suggested MRP and profit per order.

## Step 4: Choose a markup that fits your channel

| Channel | What eats the margin | Pricing implication |
|---|---|---|
| Your own website | Ads, shipping, payment fees | Highest margin if marketing is efficient |
| Marketplaces | Commission, fees, high returns | Needs a higher multiple or a separate price |
| Wholesale to boutiques | Retailer's own markup | Your wholesale price is often around half of MRP |
| Pop-ups and offline | Stall rent, travel | Good margin, low return rate |

If you plan to sell wholesale later, set an MRP that leaves room for a retailer's margin from the start.

## Step 5: Lower your costs without cutting quality

- **Avoid below-MOQ surcharges** by pooling your order. Shared setup costs keep the per-piece price close to bulk.
- **Reduce returns** with an accurate size chart and honest photos.
- **Push prepaid orders** to cut COD costs and cancellations.
- **Reorder winners** instead of carrying slow stock you later discount.

## Step 6: Sense-check against the market

Compare your price with brands at a similar quality level, not the cheapest option. If your number is higher, ask whether your fabric, fit, design and brand justify it, and make sure your product pages show why. If it is far lower, you may be leaving money on the table.

Want an accurate production cost to start your cost sheet? [Request a quote from Voz Cruda](https://vozcruda.com/#contact).

## Frequently asked questions

**What is a good markup for clothing?**
Many D2C clothing brands aim to sell at roughly three to four times their landed product cost, so there is room for marketing, returns, platform fees and profit. The right multiple depends on your channel and positioning.

**What costs should I include when pricing clothes?**
Include fabric and making, printing, labels, packaging, freight to you, sampling spread over the order, taxes, payment gateway fees, shipping to customers, returns, marketplace commissions and marketing cost per order.

**How do returns affect clothing pricing?**
Returns add reverse shipping, repacking and sometimes unsellable stock. Estimate your return rate and spread that cost across the orders you keep, especially if you sell on marketplaces.

**Does ordering in small quantities raise my cost per piece?**
Ordering alone below a factory's MOQ usually does. Pooled lots keep the per-piece price close to bulk because setup costs are shared across all buyers in the lot.

**Should I price lower than competitors to start?**
Underpricing is risky. It leaves no budget for marketing and is hard to raise later. It is usually better to justify your price with product quality, fit and brand.

# Screen Printing vs DTF vs DTG: Which Print Method Is Best for Your Clothing Brand?

URL: https://vozcruda.com/screen-printing-vs-dtf-vs-dtg-india.html
Updated: 2026-10-10

**Short answer:** Use **screen printing** for bold designs with few colours, the best durability and the lowest cost at larger quantities. Use **DTF** for small batches and multi-colour or detailed designs on most fabrics. Use **DTG** for photographic, full-colour art on cotton with a soft feel. For small brands, DTF is often the most flexible starting point.

## How each method works

- **Screen printing:** ink is pushed through a mesh screen onto the fabric, one screen per colour. Setup takes time, then printing is fast.
- **DTF (direct to film):** the design is printed onto a film with adhesive powder, then heat-pressed onto the garment.
- **DTG (direct to garment):** an inkjet printer sprays ink directly into the fabric, like a paper printer.

## Side-by-side comparison

| Factor | Screen printing | DTF | DTG |
|---|---|---|---|
| Best quantity | Moderate to large | 1 to moderate | 1 to small |
| Setup cost | Screens per colour | Low | Low |
| Colours | Few colours is cheapest | Unlimited | Unlimited |
| Detail and gradients | Limited | Very good | Excellent |
| Durability | Excellent | Very good | Good |
| Feel | Soft (water-based) to thick (plastisol) | Thin layer on top | Soft, in the fabric |
| Fabrics | Cotton, blends, many others | Cotton, polyester, blends | Mainly high-cotton |
| Dark garments | Very good | Very good | Needs pre-treatment |

## How cost changes with quantity

Screen printing has a fixed setup cost for each colour, so the price per piece falls quickly as quantity rises. DTF and DTG have almost no setup, so their price per piece stays fairly flat. That is why DTF and DTG usually win at small quantities, and screen printing wins as orders grow, especially for one or two colour designs.

Rule of thumbMany colours or small quantity: DTF or DTG. Few colours and growing quantity: screen print. Ask your manufacturer to quote both at your quantity.

## Other decoration options

- **Puff print:** a raised, textured screen print popular in streetwear.
- **Embroidery:** premium and durable for logos. Cost depends on stitch count, not colours.
- **Sublimation:** all-over prints on white polyester, common in sportswear.
- **Discharge printing:** removes dye from the fabric for a very soft vintage feel on cotton.

## Which method for which brand

| Brand situation | Good choice |
|---|---|
| First drop, multi-colour artwork, under 100 pieces | DTF |
| Photographic art on cotton tees | DTG |
| Simple logo, reorders of a bestseller | Screen print |
| Streetwear with texture | Puff print or screen print |
| Premium minimal branding | Embroidery |
| Polyester sportswear | DTF or sublimation |

## Check print quality on your sample

- Sharp edges and correct colours against your artwork.
- Placement measured from the neck seam, as in your [tech pack](https://vozcruda.com/tech-pack-guide-for-beginners.html).
- No cracking when stretched.
- Three to five washes without fading or peeling.

Not sure which method fits your design and quantity? [Send us your artwork](https://vozcruda.com/#contact) and we will suggest the best option.

## Frequently asked questions

**Which is better, DTF or screen printing?**
Screen printing is usually more durable and becomes cheaper per piece at larger quantities, especially for designs with few colours. DTF is better for small quantities and multi-colour or detailed designs because it needs no screens.

**Is DTF printing durable?**
Good-quality DTF prints are durable for many washes when applied correctly. Washing inside out in cold water and avoiding high dryer heat helps them last.

**Which print method feels softest?**
DTG and water-based screen prints feel softest because the ink sits in the fabric. DTF and plastisol screen prints sit on top of the fabric and feel slightly heavier.

**Can DTG print on polyester?**
DTG works best on high-cotton fabrics. For polyester and blends, DTF or sublimation is usually a better choice.

**What is the best print method for small batches?**
For small batches, DTF and DTG avoid screen setup costs and handle full-colour designs. For simple one or two colour logos, screen printing can still be cost-effective at moderate quantities.

# Fabric Guide for Clothing Brands: Cotton, Fleece, Terry, Linen, Blends and GSM Explained

URL: https://vozcruda.com/fabric-guide-for-clothing-brands.html
Updated: 2026-10-10

**Short answer:** Choose fabric by product and climate: cotton single jersey for tees, fleece or French terry for hoodies, linen, cotton or rayon for summer wovens, and polyester blends for activewear. **GSM** (grams per square metre) tells you the weight; for example, about 160 to 200 GSM for regular tees and 220 to 260 GSM for heavyweight oversized tees. Always confirm composition and GSM in writing and check them on the sample.

## Knits vs wovens

|  | Knit fabrics | Woven fabrics |
|---|---|---|
| How it is made | Interlocking loops | Threads crossed at right angles |
| Stretch | Natural stretch | Little or none, unless blended with spandex |
| Examples | Jersey, rib, interlock, fleece, French terry, pique | Poplin, twill, denim, linen, cambric, crepe |
| Typical products | Tees, hoodies, joggers, polos, kidswear | Shirts, trousers, kurtas, dresses, jackets |
| India hub | Tiruppur, Ludhiana, Kolkata | Surat, Bengaluru, Delhi NCR, Jaipur |

## Common knit fabrics

- **Single jersey:** the classic t-shirt fabric, smooth on one side.
- **Rib:** stretchy with visible ridges; used for cuffs, collars and fitted tops.
- **Interlock:** thicker, smooth on both sides, stable; popular for baby wear.
- **Pique:** textured, breathable; used for polo shirts.
- **French terry:** loops on the inside; for year-round sweatshirts and joggers.
- **Fleece:** brushed on the inside for warmth; for winter hoodies.

## Common woven fabrics

- **Poplin and cambric:** smooth, crisp cotton for shirts and kurtas.
- **Twill:** diagonal weave, durable; for chinos and workwear.
- **Denim:** sturdy cotton twill for jeans and jackets.
- **Linen:** very breathable with a natural texture; wrinkles easily.
- **Rayon (viscose):** soft and drapey; popular for kurtas and dresses.
- **Mulmul and voile:** very light cottons for summer wear.
- **Georgette and crepe:** flowy synthetics or blends for festive and western wear.

## Cotton quality terms

- **Carded vs combed:** combed cotton removes short fibres for a smoother, stronger fabric.
- **Bio-washed:** enzyme-treated for softness and less pilling.
- **Compacted or pre-shrunk:** processed to reduce shrinkage after washing.
- **Organic:** grown without synthetic pesticides and fertilisers; ask for certification if you market it.
- **Yarn count:** higher counts mean finer yarn and a smoother fabric.

## What GSM to choose

| Product | Typical GSM range |
|---|---|
| Light summer tee | 140 to 170 |
| Regular tee | 170 to 200 |
| Heavyweight oversized tee | 220 to 260+ |
| Polo shirt (pique) | 200 to 240 |
| Sweatshirt or French terry hoodie | 260 to 320 |
| Heavyweight fleece hoodie | 350 to 450 |

These are common ranges, not rules. Ask for a fabric swatch and feel it before deciding.

## Fabric checks before bulk production

- Weigh a swatch or sample to confirm GSM.
- Wash-test for shrinkage, colour bleeding and twisting.
- Rub-test dark colours for colour transfer.
- Check that bulk uses the same fabric lot as the approved sample.

Put your fabric choices in a [tech pack](https://vozcruda.com/tech-pack-guide-for-beginners.html), or [ask Voz Cruda](https://vozcruda.com/#contact) to recommend fabrics for your product and budget.

## Frequently asked questions

**What does GSM mean in fabric?**
GSM means grams per square metre. It measures fabric weight: a higher GSM fabric is heavier and usually thicker, while a lower GSM fabric is lighter and cooler.

**What is the difference between knit and woven fabric?**
Knit fabric is made from interlocking loops, so it stretches, like t-shirt jersey and fleece. Woven fabric is made by crossing threads at right angles, so it is more stable, like shirting, denim and linen.

**What is combed cotton?**
Combed cotton has been combed to remove short fibres and impurities before spinning. The resulting yarn is smoother and stronger, giving a softer, more even fabric than carded cotton.

**Which fabric is best for Indian summers?**
Light, breathable fabrics such as lightweight cotton jersey, cotton mulmul, linen and linen blends, and rayon work well in hot and humid weather.

**Are cotton-polyester blends good for a clothing brand?**
Blends shrink less, dry faster and cost less, which suits merchandise, team wear and activewear. Pure cotton usually feels more premium and breathable for fashion basics.

---

# The Clothing Sampling Process: Types of Samples, Costs and Timelines for New Brands

URL: https://vozcruda.com/clothing-sampling-process-india.html
Updated: 2026-10-10

**Short answer:** Clothing sampling usually moves from a **proto sample** (first version) to a **fit sample** (adjusted fit), sometimes a **size set**, and finally a **pre-production sample** made with exact bulk materials. Each round often takes one to three weeks. A clear tech pack and structured feedback are the fastest ways to fewer rounds.

## Types of samples

| Sample | Purpose | What to check |
|---|---|---|
| Proto sample | First version of the design | Overall look, construction, proportions |
| Fit sample | Refine fit on a real body | Measurements, comfort, drape |
| Size set | Check grading across sizes | Each size against the size chart |
| Pre-production (PP) sample | Final approval with bulk materials | Fabric, colour, print, labels, finishing |
| Top of production (TOP) | Pieces pulled from early bulk | Bulk matches the PP sample |

Small brands often combine steps, for example going from proto straight to PP for a simple tee with proven measurements.

## How to brief a sample

- Send a [tech pack](https://vozcruda.com/tech-pack-guide-for-beginners.html) with measurements, fabric, GSM and artwork.
- Include a reference garment if you have one with the fit you want.
- Confirm sample cost, timeline and whether it adjusts against bulk.
- Agree measurement tolerances upfront.

## How to review a sample

- **Measure** every point and record differences in a table.
- **Try it on** people of your target size. Check shoulders, chest, length and sleeve.
- **Check fabric:** GSM, hand-feel, colour.
- **Inspect construction:** seams, neck finish, hems, rib.
- **Check decoration:** placement, colours, sharpness.
- **Wash it** three to five times for shrinkage, bleeding and print durability.

## Give feedback that gets fixed

Vague comments like "make it more oversized" lead to more rounds. Give measured changes instead:

| Vague | Clear |
|---|---|
| Make it more oversized | Chest width +4 cm in all sizes, drop shoulder by 3 cm |
| Print looks too low | Move print up to 7 cm below neck seam |
| Fabric feels thin | Change to 240 GSM combed cotton |
| Neck looks off | Rib width 2 cm, reduce neck drop by 1 cm |

Mark changes on photos, update the tech pack version and send both together.

## Costs and timelines

Samples cost more per piece than bulk because each is cut and sewn individually, sometimes from fabric bought in small quantities. Each round commonly takes one to three weeks; custom fabric, dyeing or embroidery adds time. Budget for at least two rounds on a new style.

## How pooled lots shorten sampling

In a pooled lot the base garment, fabric and construction are already developed and shared. You mainly review the fit, fabric and your own print or labels, instead of developing a pattern from scratch. That can save rounds, time and sampling cost on your first drop.

## Common sampling mistakes

- Approving a sample without washing it.
- Changing several things at once without measurements.
- Skipping the PP sample, then finding bulk fabric or colour is different.
- Not keeping the approved sample as the reference for bulk checks.

Want help moving from sample to production? Read [how to vet apparel suppliers](https://vozcruda.com/how-to-vet-apparel-suppliers.html) or [talk to Voz Cruda](https://vozcruda.com/#contact).

## Frequently asked questions

**How much does a clothing sample cost in India?**
Sample costs vary with the garment, fabric and decoration. Samples cost more per piece than bulk because each one is made individually. Some factories adjust sample charges against your bulk order, so ask upfront.

**How long does garment sampling take?**
Each sample round often takes one to three weeks, depending on fabric availability and decoration. Most new styles need one or two rounds before approval.

**What is a pre-production sample?**
A pre-production (PP) sample is made with the exact bulk fabric, trims, labels and decoration. Once you approve it, it becomes the standard the bulk order is checked against.

**Do I need samples if I join a pooled order?**
In a pooled lot the base product is usually already developed, so you mainly review the fabric, fit and your own branding or print. It shortens sampling compared with developing a garment from scratch.

**How many sample rounds are normal?**
One or two rounds is common for simple products with a clear tech pack. Complex fits or new fabrics may need more. A detailed tech pack reduces rounds.

# How to Start a Streetwear Brand in India: Products, Drops and Small-Batch Production

URL: https://vozcruda.com/start-streetwear-brand-india.html
Updated: 2026-10-10

**Short answer:** To start a streetwear brand in India: define a clear identity and audience, launch two or three hero products (usually heavyweight oversized tees and hoodies), release them as small limited drops, produce in low MOQ batches, and build a community on Instagram before each drop. Small, sold-out drops protect cash and build demand.

Streetwear is built on identity, community and scarcity more than on large collections. That makes it well suited to small-batch production, as long as the product quality matches the hype.

## Step 1: Define your identity

Strong streetwear labels stand for something: a city, a music scene, skate culture, anime, sport, art or a point of view. Write down:

- Who your customer is, and where they spend time online and offline.
- The story or culture your brand comes from.
- Your visual language: graphics style, colours, typography.

## Step 2: Pick hero products

| Product | Typical spec | Why it works |
|---|---|---|
| Oversized tee | 220 to 260 GSM cotton, dropped shoulder | Lowest cost, best canvas for graphics |
| Hoodie | 320 to 450 GSM fleece or French terry | Higher price, strong brand presence |
| Joggers or shorts | French terry | Completes a set, good for repeat buyers |
| Caps and accessories | Embroidered | Low-cost add-on to orders |

Product quality is your reputation. Fabric weight, fit and print durability are what customers talk about. See our guides to [t-shirts](https://vozcruda.com/small-batch-t-shirt-manufacturing-india.html) and [hoodies](https://vozcruda.com/low-moq-hoodie-manufacturer-india.html).

## Step 3: Use the drop model

- **Design a capsule:** two to four designs that tell one story.
- **Produce small:** limited units per design.
- **Tease early:** sampling photos, behind-the-scenes, countdowns.
- **Release on a set date and time** to concentrate demand.
- **Sell out, then restock or move on,** depending on your strategy.

Drops keep stock risk low and make each release an event.

## Step 4: Choose decoration that fits the look

Streetwear graphics often use large back prints, puff print, screen print and embroidered logos. For multi-colour artwork in small runs, DTF is flexible. Compare options in [screen printing vs DTF vs DTG](https://vozcruda.com/screen-printing-vs-dtf-vs-dtg-india.html).

## Step 5: Produce in small batches

Most factories want 300 to 1,000 pieces per style for tees and hoodies, far more than a first drop needs. Pooled lots let you order the units your drop needs while getting factory quality and near-bulk pricing.

## Step 6: Build community before you sell

- Post consistently on Instagram: design process, sampling, fits, the people behind the brand.
- Work with local creators, artists, skaters and musicians who match your identity.
- Collect a waitlist before each drop through WhatsApp or email.
- Show up at flea markets, pop-ups and sneaker or culture events.

## Step 7: Price for the brand you want to be

Heavyweight fabric, good prints and branded packaging cost more, so price accordingly and include marketing and returns in your numbers. Our guide on [how to price clothing products](https://vozcruda.com/how-to-price-clothing-products.html) walks through it.

Voz Cruda runs its own streetwear label alongside sourcing, so we know these products well. [Tell us about your first drop](https://vozcruda.com/#contact).

## Frequently asked questions

**How much does it cost to start a streetwear brand in India?**
Your biggest cost is your first stock. Launching a few hero products in small quantities, through low MOQ or pooled production, keeps the starting investment much lower than a full collection.

**What products should a streetwear brand start with?**
Most streetwear labels start with heavyweight oversized tees and hoodies, sometimes adding joggers or caps. They are proven sellers and carry graphics well.

**What is a drop in streetwear?**
A drop is a limited release of a small number of designs and units, announced in advance and sold for a short time. Limited supply creates urgency and keeps stock risk low.

**How many pieces should my first drop have?**
Many new labels start with a few designs and a small number of units per design, sized to what their audience can realistically buy. Selling out small is better than discounting leftovers.

**Where can I make streetwear in India?**
Tiruppur is the main hub for heavyweight cotton tees, French terry and fleece hoodies. Voz Cruda matches labels with suitable units and pools small orders through Smallotz.

---

# Custom T-Shirts and Merchandise for Companies, Events and Teams: Small Order Guide

URL: https://vozcruda.com/custom-merchandise-small-orders-india.html
Updated: 2026-10-10

**Short answer:** For custom merchandise in small quantities, pick the product (tees, polos, hoodies or dri-fit), choose a decoration that suits the logo (embroidery for premium logos, print for large or colourful designs), collect sizes from your team, and order early. For very small runs, print on quality blanks; for custom-made pieces, pooled lots on Smallotz avoid full factory minimums.

## Who orders custom merch

- **Companies and startups:** onboarding kits, offsites, client gifts.
- **Events:** conferences, marathons, product launches, volunteers.
- **Colleges and schools:** fests, clubs, batch tees, sports teams.
- **Teams and communities:** cricket and football teams, running clubs, cafés and restaurants.

## Choose the right product

| Product | Best for | Fabric suggestion |
|---|---|---|
| Crew-neck tee | Events, fests, everyday swag | Cotton or cotton blend, 160 to 200 GSM |
| Polo shirt | Office, client-facing staff, uniforms | Pique cotton or blend |
| Hoodie or sweatshirt | Premium swag, winter offsites, college merch | French terry or fleece |
| Dri-fit tee | Sports days, marathons, outdoor events | Polyester performance fabric |
| Caps and totes | Add-ons and giveaways | Cotton twill, canvas |

## Branding options

- **Screen print:** cost-effective for simple logos as quantity grows.
- **DTF print:** flexible for multi-colour logos and small runs.
- **Embroidery:** premium, durable look for polos, caps and hoodies.
- **Sublimation:** all-over designs on polyester sportswear.

Common placements are the left chest, centre front, upper back and sleeve. Compare methods in [screen printing vs DTF vs DTG](https://vozcruda.com/screen-printing-vs-dtf-vs-dtg-india.html).

## Ready blanks vs custom-made

|  | Printing on ready blanks | Custom-made in a pooled lot |
|---|---|---|
| Quantity | Very small runs | Small runs at near-bulk pricing |
| Fabric and fit | Limited to available blanks | Better fabric, chosen fit |
| Branding | Print only, generic labels | Print, embroidery and your own labels |
| Speed | Fastest | Lot fill time plus production |

## Plan sizes properly

Wrong sizes are the most common merch complaint. Share a size chart with chest and length measurements, and collect each person's size through a simple form. If you cannot collect sizes, weight the order towards M and L and order a few spares.

## Timeline checklist

- Finalise logo files in vector format.
- Choose products, colours and placements.
- Collect sizes.
- Approve a digital mock-up and, for larger orders, a physical sample.
- Production and delivery. Build in a buffer before the event date.

Need merch for your team or event? [Send Voz Cruda your requirement](https://vozcruda.com/#contact) or [open Smallotz](https://smallotz.vozcruda.com/).

## Frequently asked questions

**Can I order custom company t-shirts in small quantities?**
Yes. Printing on ready blanks suits very small orders, and pooled production on Smallotz lets you order better quality custom-made tees and hoodies without meeting a full factory minimum.

**Which fabric is best for corporate t-shirts?**
Cotton is comfortable for everyday wear and events. Cotton-polyester blends shrink less and keep their shape, and polyester dri-fit suits sports days, marathons and outdoor events.

**How long does custom merchandise take?**
Printing on ready blanks can be quick, while custom-made garments need time for production and decoration. Plan several weeks ahead for events, and longer for large or custom orders.

**How do I decide sizes for a team order?**
Collect sizes from each person using a size chart with measurements. If that is not possible, a common approach is to weight the order towards M and L and add a few extra pieces.

**Should I choose embroidery or printing for company logos?**
Embroidery looks premium and lasts long on polos, caps and hoodies. Printing is better for large designs, event graphics and multi-colour artwork.

# How to Find Clothing Manufacturers in India: 7 Ways That Work for Small Brands

URL: https://vozcruda.com/how-to-find-clothing-manufacturers-india.html
Updated: 2026-10-10

**Short answer:** The main ways to find clothing manufacturers in India are B2B directories like IndiaMART and TradeIndia, visiting the right hub (such as Tiruppur for knitwear), trade fairs, referrals from other founders, social media, sourcing partners like Voz Cruda, and pooling platforms like Smallotz. Start from your product and quantity, build a shortlist, then verify every option with references and a paid sample.

## Before you search: know what you need

Manufacturers respond faster to specific enquiries. Have these ready:

- Product type and a few reference images
- Fabric, composition and GSM
- Quantity per style and colour
- Sizes and decoration (print, embroidery)
- Target price and timeline
- A simple [tech pack](https://vozcruda.com/tech-pack-guide-for-beginners.html), if you have one

## 7 ways to find a manufacturer

### 1. B2B directories

IndiaMART, TradeIndia and similar directories list thousands of garment suppliers searchable by product and city. They are a fast way to build a long list, but listings mix real factories with traders, so verification is essential.

### 2. Visit the right hub

Each cluster specialises: Tiruppur for knitwear, Surat for synthetics and ethnic fabrics, Jaipur for prints, Ludhiana for winterwear, Delhi NCR for fashion and private label. Visiting lets you see many units in a few days. See [India's garment hubs](https://vozcruda.com/india-apparel-manufacturing-hubs.html), or our [Tiruppur guide](https://vozcruda.com/tiruppur-garment-manufacturing-guide.html) for knitwear.

### 3. Trade fairs and exhibitions

Textile and apparel fairs bring manufacturers, fabric mills and trim suppliers under one roof. They are useful for meeting many suppliers at once, though many exhibitors target large buyers.

### 4. Referrals from other founders

Founder communities, WhatsApp groups and industry contacts often point to the most reliable units. Ask what the factory does well, and what went wrong.

### 5. Social media and LinkedIn

Many manufacturers now post production videos on Instagram and LinkedIn. It is a good way to see real work, but still verify before ordering.

### 6. Sourcing partners

A sourcing partner like Voz Cruda matches your product and quantity with manufacturers whose capability fits, then coordinates sampling and production through one point of contact. It saves weeks of searching and vetting.

### 7. Order pooling platforms

If your quantity is below a factory's minimum, pooling platforms combine your order with other buyers. You get access to factories that would otherwise decline your order.

## Compare the options

| Method | Speed | Vetting effort | Good for small quantities |
|---|---|---|---|
| B2B directories | Fast | High | Sometimes |
| Hub visits | Medium | Medium | Sometimes |
| Trade fairs | Depends on dates | Medium | Less often |
| Referrals | Varies | Lower | Often |
| Social media | Fast | High | Sometimes |
| Sourcing partner (Voz Cruda) | Fast | Done for you | Yes |
| Pooling (Smallotz) | Lot fill time | Done for you | Yes, built for it |

## Write an enquiry that gets a reply

Example enquiryHi, we are a D2C streetwear brand in Bengaluru. We need oversized tees in 240 GSM combed cotton, 3 colours, sizes S to XXL, 150 pieces per colour, with a large back screen print. Target delivery in 8 weeks. Tech pack attached. Could you share your MOQ, price at this quantity, sample cost and lead time?

## Then shortlist and verify

Narrow your list to three to five manufacturers, compare quotes on the same specification, and run each through our [supplier vetting checklist](https://vozcruda.com/how-to-vet-apparel-suppliers.html) before paying for samples.

Want to skip the search? [Tell Voz Cruda what you want to make](https://vozcruda.com/#contact) and we will match you with suitable manufacturers.

## Frequently asked questions

**How do I find a clothing manufacturer in India for a small brand?**
Start from your product and quantity. Use B2B directories and hub visits to build a shortlist, ask for references and samples, or use a sourcing partner like Voz Cruda that matches small brands with suitable manufacturers.

**Are IndiaMART suppliers reliable?**
B2B directories list many genuine manufacturers alongside traders and middlemen. Treat a listing as a starting point and verify GST details, the factory, references and a sample before ordering.

**How do I contact a clothing manufacturer?**
Send a short, specific enquiry: product, fabric and GSM, quantity per style, sizes, decoration, target price and timeline, with a tech pack or reference images. Specific enquiries get faster, more accurate replies.

**Why do manufacturers not reply to small brands?**
Many factories prioritise orders that meet their MOQ. Clear enquiries help, and pooled orders or a sourcing partner can get small brands a response by bringing combined volume.

**Should I visit the factory?**
If you can, yes. A visit, or at least a live video walk-through, shows real capability, working conditions and quality control far better than photos.

# Tech Pack Example: A Complete T-Shirt Tech Pack, Page by Page

URL: https://vozcruda.com/tech-pack-example-t-shirt.html
Updated: 2026-10-24

**Short answer:** A complete t-shirt tech pack has eight parts: a cover page, front and back flat sketches, a size chart with tolerances, a bill of materials, construction details, artwork and placement, labels and packing, and an order sheet. Below is each part filled in for an example oversized cotton tee, which you can adapt for your own style.

Our [beginner's guide to tech packs](https://vozcruda.com/tech-pack-guide-for-beginners.html) explains what a tech pack is and why it matters. This page is the practical companion: a worked example you can follow line by line. The style, numbers and materials are an illustration for a typical oversized tee, not a standard. Use your own reference garment for your measurements.

## Page 1: Cover

| Brand | Your brand name |
| Style name | Oversized Heavy Tee |
| Style number | TS-001 |
| Season or drop | Drop 01 |
| Version and date | V1, first issue |
| Sizes | S, M, L, XL |
| Contact | Name, phone and email of the person who approves samples |

**Why it matters:** the style number and version are how you and the factory refer to this exact garment. When a sample comes back, you will review it against "TS-001 V1" and issue "V2" with the changes, so nobody works from an old file.

## Page 2: Flat sketches

Two simple line drawings, front and back, drawn as if the tee is lying flat. No model, no shading. Add arrows and short callouts for each detail:

- Dropped shoulder seam
- 2 cm 1x1 rib neck, with self-fabric back neck tape
- Single-needle topstitch at neck rib
- 2.5 cm twin-needle hem on body and sleeves
- Front print position (see page 6) and printed neck label position (see page 7)

**Why it matters:** callouts tell the sampling tailor what is intentional. Without "dropped shoulder" on the sketch, a factory used to regular fits may correct it for you.

## Page 3: Size chart and tolerances

All measurements in centimetres, garment measured flat. The numbers below are an example for a boxy oversized fit.

| Point of measure | S | M | L | XL | Tolerance |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A. Half chest, 2 cm below armhole | 56 | 58.5 | 61 | 63.5 | ± 1 |
| B. Body length, from high point of shoulder | 70 | 72 | 74 | 76 | ± 1 |
| C. Shoulder width, seam to seam | 54 | 56 | 58 | 60 | ± 1 |
| D. Sleeve length, from shoulder seam | 22 | 23 | 24 | 25 | ± 0.5 |
| E. Half sleeve opening | 20 | 21 | 22 | 23 | ± 0.5 |
| F. Armhole, straight | 25 | 26 | 27 | 28 | ± 0.5 |
| G. Neck width, seam to seam | 19 | 19.5 | 20 | 20.5 | ± 0.5 |
| H. Front neck drop | 9 | 9 | 9.5 | 9.5 | ± 0.5 |
| I. Neck rib width | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | ± 0.2 |
| J. Half hem width | 56 | 58.5 | 61 | 63.5 | ± 1 |

Add a small diagram with letters A to J so the factory's quality checker measures the same way you do.

TipTolerances are tighter on small details like rib width and neck drop, because a 1 cm difference there is easy to see. Body measurements can usually take a little more.

**Why it matters:** this table is what the finished garments are checked against. "Fits a bit small" is an opinion. "Half chest 55 cm against 58.5 ± 1" is a defect.

## Page 4: Bill of materials

| Item | Specification | Colour | Where used |
|---|---|---|---|
| Main fabric | 100% combed cotton single jersey, 240 GSM, bio-washed, pre-shrunk | Black, off-white | Body and sleeves |
| Rib | 1x1 cotton rib, matched to body colour | Match body | Neck |
| Back neck tape | Self fabric, 1 cm | Match body | Inside back neck |
| Sewing thread | Spun polyester | Match body | All seams |
| Care label | Printed satin, sewn into left side seam | White | Inside left side seam |

**Why it matters:** GSM, composition and finish change both the feel and the price. "Cotton tee" could be quoted at 160 GSM or 260 GSM. See our [fabric and GSM guide](https://vozcruda.com/fabric-guide-for-clothing-brands.html) if these terms are new.

## Page 5: Construction

- **Shoulder seams:** 4-thread overlock with tape for stability.
- **Side seams:** 4-thread overlock, no side slits.
- **Sleeve attach:** 4-thread overlock.
- **Neck:** rib attached with overlock, single-needle topstitch on body side.
- **Hems:** body and sleeve hems 2.5 cm, twin-needle coverstitch.
- **Stitch density:** state your expectation, or ask the factory for its standard and record it here.

**Why it matters:** hem width and neck finish are some of the most visible signs of quality on a tee, and they are easy to change silently between sample and bulk if they are not written down.

## Page 6: Artwork and placement

| Method | Screen print, water-based ink |
| Artwork file | TS-001_front_V1 (vector PDF, separate attachment) |
| Print size | 28 cm wide x 20 cm high on size M; same size on all sizes |
| Placement | Centred, top of artwork 8 cm below front neck seam |
| Colours | One colour, off-white on black body (give a Pantone reference or send a swatch) |

Show the artwork on the flat sketch with the 8 cm measurement drawn in. If you want the print to scale by size, say so and give the size for each one.

**Why it matters:** "print on chest" means something different to every printer. Measured placement makes it repeatable across sizes and reorders. If you are still choosing a method, compare [screen printing, DTF and DTG](https://vozcruda.com/screen-printing-vs-dtf-vs-dtg-india.html).

## Page 7: Labels and packing

- **Neck label:** printed inside back neck, brand logo and size, 6 cm wide, centred 2 cm below neck seam.
- **Care label:** fibre content, wash care symbols, country of origin, inside left side seam 8 cm above hem.
- **Hang tag:** attached at left sleeve hem with a tag pin or string, if you use one.
- **Fold:** folded with print facing out, size label visible.
- **Polybag:** one piece per polybag with size sticker; state your polybag type if you have a preference.
- **Cartons:** packed by size, with carton marking showing style number, colour, size and quantity.

**Why it matters:** labels and packing are often the last thing a new brand thinks about and the first thing that delays dispatch. Custom labels can have their own minimums and lead times, so order them early.

## Page 8: Order sheet

| Colour | S | M | L | XL | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Black | 15 | 25 | 25 | 15 | 80 |
| Off-white | 10 | 15 | 15 | 10 | 50 |
| **Total** | 25 | 40 | 40 | 25 | **130** |

Add your target delivery date and address. A size split weighted towards M and L is a common starting point for unisex oversized tees, but use your own sales data if you have it.

At 130 pieces, this order sits below many factories' minimums. That is where pooling helps: the base tee is shared with other buyers so the lot reaches the factory MOQ, and your tech pack only needs the parts that are yours.

## What to change for your own style

- **Regular fit tee:** reduce half chest and shoulder, raise the shoulder seam to the natural shoulder, shorten body length slightly.
- **Hoodie or sweatshirt:** add hood height and width, cuff and waistband rib measurements, pocket position, drawcord and eyelet details. See our [hoodie guide](https://vozcruda.com/low-moq-hoodie-manufacturer-india.html).
- **Embroidery instead of print:** give stitch count or ask the embroiderer for it, thread colours, and backing type.
- **All-over or sleeve prints:** add a placement drawing for each panel.

Want this example as a file? [Download the free tech pack template](https://vozcruda.com/tech-pack-template.html), including this t-shirt example filled in as an Excel sheet.

## Before you send it

- Check every page has the same style number and version.
- Check every measuring point has a value for every size and a tolerance.
- Attach artwork as separate files, not only as pictures inside the PDF.
- Send it with your quantity and target date so the factory can quote properly.

Then follow the [sampling process](https://vozcruda.com/clothing-sampling-process-india.html): review the first sample against this tech pack point by point and issue V2 with changes. [Share your tech pack with Voz Cruda](https://vozcruda.com/#contact) and we will match it with a suitable manufacturer.

## Frequently asked questions

**Can I copy this tech pack example for my own t-shirt?**
Yes, use it as a starting structure. Replace the measurements with ones taken from a reference garment you like, and change the fabric, artwork and labels to match your product. The example numbers are illustrative, not a standard size chart.

**What measurements are needed for a t-shirt tech pack?**
At minimum: half chest, body length from high point of shoulder, shoulder width, sleeve length, sleeve opening, armhole, neck width, front neck drop, rib width and hem width, each with a tolerance.

**How do I specify print placement in a tech pack?**
Give the artwork size in centimetres and measure its position from a fixed point on the garment, such as 8 cm below the front neck seam and centred. Add a drawing showing the placement on the flat sketch.

**Should the size chart be in centimetres or inches?**
Either works if you are consistent, but most Indian garment factories work in centimetres or accept both. State the unit at the top of the size chart.

**Does the factory need my tech pack in a specific format?**
No. A clear PDF is the safest choice because it keeps the layout fixed. Send the artwork as separate high-resolution or vector files alongside it.
