# How to Negotiate MOQ with Clothing Manufacturers: 9 Tactics That Work

URL: https://vozcruda.com/how-to-negotiate-moq-clothing-manufacturers.html
Updated: 2026-10-24

**Short answer:** To negotiate a lower MOQ, find out what is driving the minimum and remove it. Use the factory's stock fabric, cut down on colours, share one fabric across styles, keep trims standard, offer a reorder plan or a flexible delivery date, or accept a modest surcharge. If none of that works, pool your order with other buyers so the lot meets the factory minimum.

New brands often treat an MOQ like a price tag: take it or leave it. In practice it is the factory's way of protecting itself from fixed costs it cannot spread over a small order. If your request avoids those costs, or covers them another way, the number usually has room to move.

If you are new to the term, start with our guide to [low MOQ clothing manufacturing in India](https://vozcruda.com/low-moq-clothing-manufacturers-india.html), which explains the different kinds of minimum and why factories set them.

## First, ask what the MOQ is based on

Before negotiating anything, ask one question: "Is this minimum for the stitching, the fabric, the print, or the trims?" The answer tells you where to push.

| If the MOQ comes from | What usually brings it down |
|---|---|
| Fabric or dye lot | Stock colours, running fabrics, sharing fabric across styles |
| Print or embroidery setup | Fewer colours in the artwork, one design across styles, a different print method |
| Custom trims | Standard trims for the first order, printed instead of woven labels |
| Line setup and capacity | Flexible dates, simpler construction, a reorder plan |

## 9 ways to get a lower MOQ

### 1. Choose stock or running fabric

Custom-dyed fabric often has its own minimum from the dyeing unit or mill, and that minimum then sets yours. Ask which fabrics and colours the factory already runs. Black, white, navy, grey melange and a few seasonal shades are commonly available in basic knits, which can remove the fabric minimum entirely.

### 2. Order fewer colours

Per-colour minimums multiply fast. Three colours at 100 pieces each is 300 pieces; one colour at 150 might be accepted. Launch in your best colour and add others when it sells.

### 3. Use one fabric across several styles

If a tee and a longline tee, or a hoodie and a sweatshirt, share the same fleece, the factory can buy one larger fabric lot. Some factories will then accept lower quantities per style because the fabric total meets their minimum.

### 4. Keep trims and labels standard for the first run

Custom zips, woven labels, branded drawcord tips and special buttons each carry their own minimums and lead times. A printed neck label and standard trims for your first order keep things moving. Upgrade once the style has proved itself.

### 5. Simplify the print

In screen printing, each colour usually needs its own screen and setup. A one or two colour design is cheaper to set up than a six colour one. For small quantities of complex artwork, ask whether DTF suits the design instead. Our comparison of [screen printing vs DTF vs DTG](https://vozcruda.com/screen-printing-vs-dtf-vs-dtg-india.html) explains the trade-offs.

### 6. Be flexible on timing

Factories have busy and quiet periods. If your order can slot into a gap between larger orders, a smaller quantity is easier to accept. Saying "we are flexible on the delivery date by two or three weeks" is a real concession.

### 7. Offer a clear reorder plan

A factory takes a small first order more seriously when it can see the next one. Share your plan honestly, for example "120 pieces now, and we expect to reorder this style within three months if it sells." Do not promise volumes you cannot commit to; factories remember.

### 8. Accept a small surcharge

Many factories will produce below MOQ for a higher price per piece, which covers setup costs over fewer units. Before you agree, check that your margin still works using our [clothing pricing guide](https://vozcruda.com/how-to-price-clothing-products.html). A surcharge that is fine on a premium hoodie may break the numbers on a basic tee.

### 9. Pool your order with other buyers

If the factory will not move, change who makes up the minimum. In a pooled lot, several brands order the same base product, and the combined quantity meets the factory MOQ. Each brand pays near-bulk pricing for only its own quantity. Read [how MOQ aggregation works](https://vozcruda.com/what-is-moq-aggregation.html).

## A message you can send

Keep it short, specific and easy to say yes to. Factories get many vague enquiries, and a clear one stands out.

TemplateHello, we are a new brand based in [city] looking to make [product], [fabric and GSM], in [colours]. Our first order is [quantity] pieces across sizes [S to XL]. We understand your usual minimum is higher. To make a smaller order work, we can use one of your running fabrics and colours, keep trims standard, and be flexible on delivery by two to three weeks. If it sells, we plan to reorder this style. Could you let us know the lowest quantity you could accept on those terms, and the price at that quantity and at your standard MOQ? Our tech pack is attached.

Attaching a tech pack shows you are serious and lets the factory quote accurately. If you do not have one yet, our [tech pack guide](https://vozcruda.com/tech-pack-guide-for-beginners.html) and [t-shirt tech pack example](https://vozcruda.com/tech-pack-example-t-shirt.html) will help.

## What not to do

- **Do not ask for bulk pricing at sample quantities.** Ask for the price at your quantity and at their MOQ, so you can see the real difference.
- **Do not hide your quantity.** Factories quote better when they know the real number.
- **Do not promise future volumes you cannot commit to.**
- **Do not skip the sample** to save money on a small order. A rejected bulk order costs far more. See the [sampling process](https://vozcruda.com/clothing-sampling-process-india.html).
- **Do not negotiate only on WhatsApp.** Confirm the agreed quantity, price, size split and date on a purchase order.

## When to stop negotiating

If the price at your quantity makes the product unprofitable, or the factory agrees but shows little interest in your order, it may be the wrong fit. A factory that sees your order as a nuisance tends to slot it last. It is usually better to find a smaller unit, a factory with a running product close to yours, or a pooled lot. [Tell Voz Cruda what you want to make](https://vozcruda.com/#contact) and we can suggest the route that suits your quantity.

## Frequently asked questions

**Can you negotiate MOQ with a clothing manufacturer?**
Often, yes. Most minimums come from fabric, dyeing, printing or trim costs. If you choose stock fabric, fewer colours or standard trims, or accept a small surcharge, many factories will accept a lower quantity.

**What is the easiest way to get a lower MOQ?**
Use the factory's stock or running fabric instead of a custom colour. Fabric and dye lot minimums are the most common reason a garment MOQ is high.

**Is a per-colour MOQ negotiable?**
Sometimes. Fewer colours is the simplest fix, but some factories will accept lower per-colour quantities if the total for the style stays at their minimum, or if the colours are ones they already run.

**Should I pay a surcharge to order below MOQ?**
It can be worth it for a first order you need quickly, as long as your margin still works at the higher price. Run the numbers with your landed cost and selling price before agreeing.

**What if the factory will not lower its MOQ?**
Ask for a referral to a smaller unit, look for a factory with a running product close to yours, or join a pooled lot where other buyers make up the rest of the minimum.

---

# Tiruppur Garment Manufacturing: A Buyer's Guide for Small Brands

URL: https://vozcruda.com/tiruppur-garment-manufacturing-guide.html
Updated: 2026-10-24

**Short answer:** **Tiruppur**, in western Tamil Nadu near Coimbatore, is India's best-known hub for cotton knitwear: t-shirts, polos, hoodies, sweatshirts, joggers, innerwear and kidswear. It works as a cluster of specialised units for knitting, dyeing, printing, stitching and packing, coordinated by a manufacturer or merchant. Small brands can source there through smaller units, a sourcing partner, or pooled orders that meet a factory's minimum.

Our overview of [India's garment hubs](https://vozcruda.com/india-apparel-manufacturing-hubs.html) explains what each city specialises in. This guide goes deeper on the one most small apparel brands start with, because almost every new label's first product is a tee or a hoodie.

## What Tiruppur makes best

| Product | Common fabrics | Good fit for Tiruppur? |
|---|---|---|
| T-shirts, regular and oversized | Single jersey, 160 to 260 GSM | Yes, the core product |
| Polos | Pique | Yes |
| Hoodies, sweatshirts, joggers | French terry, fleece | Yes |
| Kidswear and baby wear | Soft single jersey, interlock, rib | Yes |
| Innerwear and loungewear | Jersey, rib, cotton-elastane blends | Yes |
| Woven shirts, denim, tailored trousers | Wovens | Usually better elsewhere |
| Heavy woollen winterwear | Wool, acrylic knits | Usually Ludhiana |

If you are new to GSM and knit types, our [fabric guide](https://vozcruda.com/fabric-guide-for-clothing-brands.html) explains them.

## How the Tiruppur cluster works

A buyer usually deals with one manufacturer, but the garment often passes through several specialised units before it is finished. Understanding this helps you ask better questions.

- **Yarn** is bought from spinning mills.
- **Knitting units** turn yarn into greige (undyed) fabric on circular knitting machines.
- **Dyeing and processing units** dye, wash and finish the fabric, including compacting to control shrinkage.
- **Cutting and stitching** happen at the manufacturer's own unit or with a job-work stitching unit.
- **Printing and embroidery** are often done by separate specialist units.
- **Checking, ironing and packing** finish the order.

Some larger factories do several of these steps in-house. Many smaller manufacturers coordinate job-work units for the rest. Neither is automatically better. What matters is that the person you deal with controls quality across every step.

Ask this"Which steps do you do in-house, and which go to job-work units?" A clear answer shows the manufacturer knows its own supply chain. It also tells you where delays are most likely, since each handover adds time.

## MOQs and pricing in Tiruppur

Many Tiruppur units are built for export and large domestic orders, so minimums of several hundred pieces per style are common, often with per-colour minimums too. The ranges in our [low MOQ guide](https://vozcruda.com/low-moq-clothing-manufacturers-india.html) are a good guide to what you will hear.

The biggest drivers of price per piece are:

- **Fabric:** yarn quality (combed or carded cotton), GSM and any special finish such as bio-wash.
- **Colour:** running colours are cheaper and faster than custom dyed shades.
- **Print or embroidery:** method, size and number of colours.
- **Quantity:** setup costs spread across fewer pieces push the price up.
- **Trims and packing:** custom labels, tags and packaging.

Small brands often get the best results by choosing a running fabric and colour, keeping the first print simple, and pooling quantity with other buyers. Our guide on [how to negotiate MOQ](https://vozcruda.com/how-to-negotiate-moq-clothing-manufacturers.html) covers more tactics.

## Lead times

For basic tees and fleece, plan for sampling first, then several weeks of production after you approve the sample. Lead times stretch when the fabric needs a custom dye, when artwork needs several sampling rounds, or during peak seasons when units are full with large orders. Ask for a dated plan with fabric, sample approval, production and dispatch milestones. Our [sampling guide](https://vozcruda.com/clothing-sampling-process-india.html) explains each stage.

## Sourcing from Tiruppur remotely

You do not need to visit to work with a Tiruppur manufacturer. A remote process that works:

- Send a clear [tech pack](https://vozcruda.com/tech-pack-guide-for-beginners.html) with your quantity and target date.
- Ask for fabric swatches or a photo and GSM reading of the running fabric.
- Approve a sample by courier, measured against your size chart.
- Get a video walk-through of the unit and a mid-production update with photos.
- Check a sample of finished pieces before final payment, or use a third-party inspection.

Delivery within India is usually by road transport or courier. Agree who arranges and pays for it before production starts.

## If you do visit

- **Fly into Coimbatore** and travel to Tiruppur by road.
- **Bring your tech pack and reference garments.** Touching fabric in person is the fastest way to agree a quality level.
- **Visit more than one unit,** including the stitching floor, not only the office and showroom.
- **Look for** organised cutting tables, measurement checks on the line, clean storage of finished goods and a quality checker with your spec sheet.
- **Ask to see** a current order for another brand at a similar quantity to yours.

Our [supplier vetting checklist](https://vozcruda.com/how-to-vet-apparel-suppliers.html) covers what to check and the red flags to watch for.

## Is Tiruppur right for your brand?

If your range is built around cotton knits, such as tees, polos, sweatshirts, hoodies, joggers or kidswear, Tiruppur is usually the right place to start. If you mainly make woven shirts, denim, structured womenswear or ethnic wear, another hub will usually suit you better. Either way, [tell Voz Cruda what you want to make](https://vozcruda.com/#contact) and we will match you with a suitable unit, or open [Smallotz](https://smallotz.vozcruda.com/) to join a pooled lot.

## Frequently asked questions

**Why is Tiruppur famous for garments?**
Tiruppur has built a complete cotton knitwear chain in one region over several decades, from knitting and dyeing to printing, stitching and packing. That depth of skills and suppliers makes it efficient for t-shirts, polos, innerwear, kidswear and fleece.

**Where is Tiruppur?**
Tiruppur is in western Tamil Nadu, close to Coimbatore. Most buyers fly into Coimbatore and travel to Tiruppur by road.

**Can I order small quantities from Tiruppur manufacturers?**
Some smaller units accept small orders, usually at a higher price per piece. Many export-focused factories have higher minimums. Pooled lots on Smallotz let small brands reach a Tiruppur factory's MOQ by combining orders with other buyers.

**Is Tiruppur good for hoodies and sweatshirts?**
Yes. Tiruppur units make French terry and fleece garments such as hoodies, sweatshirts and joggers alongside t-shirts. Heavier winterwear and woollens are more often sourced from Ludhiana.

**Do I need to visit Tiruppur to source from it?**
No. Many brands work remotely using a tech pack, samples by courier and video calls, or through a sourcing partner. A visit helps when you are placing larger or repeat orders and want to see the unit for yourself.

# How Garment Manufacturers in India Can Find Buyers: A Practical Guide

URL: https://vozcruda.com/how-garment-manufacturers-find-buyers-india.html
Updated: 2026-10-24

**Short answer:** Garment manufacturers in India find buyers mainly through **referrals**, **B2B marketplaces**, **trade fairs**, **buying agents and sourcing partners**, and **direct outreach** to brands whose products match their capability. Bought lists of "garment buyer contact details" rarely work. A clear capability sheet sent to the right brands works much better.

Most of our guides are written for brands looking for a factory. This one is for the other side of the table: the factory owner, merchant or production head who has capacity and wants more of the right orders. It draws on what buyers tell us they look for when choosing a manufacturer.

## Why buyer contact lists rarely work

It is tempting to buy a spreadsheet of thousands of "garment buyers" and email them all. In practice:

- **The contacts are often outdated** or generic inboxes that nobody in sourcing reads.
- **They are rarely the decision maker.** At small brands the founder decides; at larger ones a sourcing or production manager does.
- **Mass emails look like spam,** and sending them can hurt your email domain's reputation.
- **Most of the brands will not match what you make.** A knitwear unit gets nowhere pitching a denim brand.

Twenty well-chosen brands contacted personally usually do more than two thousand cold emails.

## Know which buyers suit your unit

Before looking for buyers, write down who you are actually good for. It makes every channel below work better.

| Buyer type | Typical order | What they value |
|---|---|---|
| New and D2C brands | Small quantities, frequent reorders | Low MOQ, help with sampling, clear communication |
| Boutiques and retailers | Small to medium, seasonal | Reliable dates, consistent quality |
| Private label and wholesale buyers | Medium to large, repeat styles | Price, consistency, capacity |
| Corporate and event merchandise | One-off, fixed deadline | Speed, printing and embroidery |
| Export buyers and buying houses | Large, compliance-led | Certifications, audits, documentation |

A unit that is excellent at 200-piece runs of premium tees should chase D2C brands, not large export programmes, and the other way round.

## 8 channels that bring in real orders

### 1. Referrals from current customers

Happy buyers are your best salespeople. Ask them directly who else they know who is launching or scaling, and deliver well on small orders: small brands talk to each other constantly.

### 2. B2B marketplaces and directories

Platforms such as IndiaMART and TradeIndia are where many domestic buyers start searching. A listing works when it is specific: real photos of your work, products and fabrics you make, MOQ and a fast response. Generic listings with stock photos get ignored.

### 3. Trade fairs and industry events

Apparel and textile fairs, including events organised by export promotion bodies such as AEPC, put you in front of buyers who are actively sourcing. Bring samples, a printed capability sheet and a clear answer to "what is your MOQ?"

### 4. Buying agents and buying houses

Agents and buying houses connect brands, often international, with factories. They take a commission or margin, but can bring steady volume if your compliance and quality match their buyers' needs.

### 5. Sourcing partners and pooled-order platforms

Sourcing companies match brands with factories and coordinate production. Pooled-order platforms go further for small buyers: they combine many small orders into one that meets your MOQ, so you get factory-sized orders from brands that could never place one alone. Voz Cruda does both, through supplier matching and [MOQ aggregation on Smallotz](https://vozcruda.com/what-is-moq-aggregation.html).

### 6. Direct outreach to brands that fit

Look at Instagram, marketplaces and D2C websites for brands selling the kind of product you make well. Find the founder or sourcing contact on their website or LinkedIn, and send a short, personal message (template below).

### 7. Your own website and Google Business Profile

Many buyers search on Google for terms like "t-shirt manufacturer in Tiruppur" or "kurta manufacturer Jaipur". A simple website with your products, capacity, photos and contact details, plus a complete Google Business Profile with real photos, helps you appear in those searches.

### 8. Wholesale markets and local networks

For domestic wholesale and retail buyers, local markets, associations and traders in your hub remain important. They often lead to steady repeat business on running styles.

## The capability sheet buyers want

A one or two page PDF that answers a buyer's first questions before they ask. Include:

- **What you make:** product types, fabrics and GSM ranges, and what you do not make.
- **Processes in-house vs outsourced:** knitting, dyeing, cutting, stitching, printing, embroidery, finishing.
- **MOQ:** per style and per colour, and whether you accept pooled or smaller orders.
- **Capacity and lead times:** realistic monthly capacity and typical time from sample approval to dispatch.
- **Sampling:** sample cost, time, and whether it is adjusted against bulk.
- **Photos:** your actual unit and finished pieces, not stock images.
- **Certifications and compliance,** if you have them, such as GST registration and any audits or fabric certifications.
- **A named contact** with phone, WhatsApp and email.

Buyers check suppliers carefully. Our guide on [how brands vet apparel suppliers](https://vozcruda.com/how-to-vet-apparel-suppliers.html) shows what they will look for, so you can prepare for it.

## A message you can send to a brand

TemplateHello [name], I am [your name] from [unit name] in [city]. We make [products] in [fabrics and GSM range], and work with brands ordering from [your MOQ] pieces per style. I noticed your [product] range and think our [specific capability] could suit it. I have attached a short capability sheet with photos of our recent work. Happy to send a sample of something similar if useful.

Keep it short, mention something specific about their brand, and offer a sample instead of a long pitch.

## Win the reorder, not just the first order

- **Share a dated production plan** and update it without being chased.
- **Flag problems early.** Buyers forgive a delay they hear about in advance far more than one they discover.
- **Match the approved sample** in bulk. Quiet substitutions in fabric or trims lose buyers.
- **Pack and label exactly as asked.** It is the first thing the buyer sees when the carton opens.

## Frequently asked questions

**Where can I find garment buyer contact details?**
Public contact details for brands are usually on their websites and LinkedIn pages. Lists sold as buyer databases are often outdated and the contacts are rarely the person who places orders. Targeted outreach to brands that fit your capability works better than mass emailing a list.

**How do small garment factories find buyers in India?**
Through referrals from existing customers, B2B marketplaces, trade fairs, buying agents, direct outreach to D2C brands and boutiques, a clear website and Google Business Profile, and sourcing partners that match factories with buyers.

**What do buyers want to see from a garment manufacturer?**
A short capability sheet: the products and fabrics you make, MOQ, monthly capacity, lead times, sample policy, photos of the unit and of finished work, certifications if any, and a named contact who replies quickly.

**Can small orders be worth it for a factory?**
They can if they fill gaps in capacity or lead to repeat orders. Pooled orders help here: several small buyers combine quantities into one order that meets your MOQ.
